copies.headline: Noah's Backfield Can't Cover Three Positions
copies.body:
Noah wins the running back battle and loses everywhere else. Achane and Cook at 18 and 15 is a real edge, but Achane is landing in Miami-Las Vegas, a 40.5 total with the Dolphins as underdogs, which is the kind of game that produces 11 touches and a shrug. Everything above that gets ugly: Drake Maye in Seattle, Colston Loveland at 12 against John's choice of Brock Bowers (16) or Trey McBride (14), and a receiver room built on questionable tags. Mike Evans and Josh Downs are both flagged, and behind them it's Michael Wilson and Romeo Doubs. The #12 power ranking isn't an insult, it's arithmetic.
John's points come from the best game on the board. Stafford, Kyren Williams and Puka Nacua all sit in Rams-49ers with a 48.5 total, which is a lot of eggs in one basket but a very good basket. Nacua's questionable tag is the only thing standing between John and a comfortable Sunday, and Brian Thomas Jr. plus Quentin Johnston are functional insurance. Bowers and McBride at tight end means John can bench a 14-point player.

copies.headline: Isaac's Receivers Are All Wearing Question Marks
copies.body:
Isaac wins the wideout column on paper — Ja'Marr Chase, Malik Nabers and Terry McLaurin give him 46 to Kaleb's 41 — but five of his seven receivers carry a questionable tag, including Chase, Nabers and DK Metcalf. Strip one of those out and the depth behind it is Adonai Mitchell at 8. Kaleb gives the edge back everywhere else: Justin Herbert (19) over Bo Nix (16), Ashton Jeanty and Breece Hall (35) over Javonte Williams and Cam Skattebo (29), Harold Fannin (11) over T.J. Hockenson (9). That's +11 across three spots against a +5 that depends on medical reports.
The game environments favor Kaleb too. Nix is at Kansas City in a 42.5 total, the lowest-scoring spot on either roster, while Herbert gets Arizona as a 10.5-point favorite. Chase in a 50.5-total game is Isaac's real ceiling, and Nabers should see volume with the Giants chasing Dallas. Kaleb, ranked 4th to Isaac's 10th, just needs his running backs to suit up.

copies.headline: Grant's Receivers Beat CJ's Injury Report
copies.body:
Two teams separated by one power ranking slot and about two projected points, which means the difference is receiver certainty. Grant's top three go 45 to CJ's 39, and more importantly they're actually functional: Amon-Ra St. Brown (19) in a 49.5-total game Detroit is favored by seven, Jaylen Waddle, Christian Watson in a Minnesota-Green Bay coin flip. CJ's wideout room is Rashee Rice at 14 and then a pile of question marks — Emeka Egbuka questionable in a 50.5-total shootout at Cincinnati, Alec Pierce questionable, Parker Washington as the only healthy third option worth starting.
Backfields are a dead heat at 31, though CJ's is held together with tape: Pacheco on IR, Charbonnet out, Hubbard and Henderson questionable, leaving Jonathan Taylor and Quinshon Judkins to carry it. Joe Burrow's 18 in a 50.5-point game is CJ's real edge and his best path to a shootout ceiling. Grant just needs Zay Flowers to clear his tag; Baker Mayfield sitting on the bench at 16 is insurance nobody else in this game has.

copies.headline: Logan's Eagles Stack Outguns Adam's Depth
copies.body:
The whole thing runs through Philadelphia. Logan has Jalen Hurts (21) and Saquon Barkley (18) in a game his own opponent's quarterback is playing in — Adam counters with Jayden Daniels (17) as a 4.5-point road underdog, which at least means late throwing volume in a 45.5-total game. But Logan's top two backs project 32 to Adam's 27, and Kenneth Walker III against Denver in a 42.5-total game is the least appealing environment on either roster. Adam's edges are real but small: 46 to 44 at receiver on the strength of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Chris Olave chasing points down seven in Detroit, and Rome Odunze, plus two points at tight end.
The risk profile favors Logan anyway. Jeremiyah Love, Michael Pittman Jr., Luther Burden III and De'Zhaun Stribling all carry tags, but Logan has thirteen bodies at RB/WR to absorb it. Adam has Sam LaPorta questionable with Mark Andrews right behind him, which is fine, and five receivers total, two of whom project single digits. Thin roster, decent lineup.

copies.headline: Peter's Tight End Is A Coin Flip
copies.body:
Two points separate these projections, which means the decision comes from the questionable tags, and Peter has more of them. Tucker Kraft is his only tight end — if the Packers hold him out at Minnesota, Peter is starting nothing at the position while Christian falls back on Chig Okonkwo. Tee Higgins is the other one that matters, and he's in the week's best game environment (Cincinnati-Tampa, 50.5). Christian's tags are cushioned: Kittle out means Okonkwo slides up, Shakir and Tuten are depth pieces on a roster that's five deep at both receiver and running back.
The top-end talent favors Peter — Lamar Jackson in a 48.5 at Indianapolis, Bijan Robinson, A.J. Brown — but Bijan's Falcons are three-point dogs in a 41.5 game, the lowest-scoring script on either roster. Christian's points come from Dallas-New York and Philadelphia-Washington, cleaner totals with CeeDee Lamb, DeVonta Smith and Brandon Aubrey attached. Trevor Lawrence in a 40.5 is the soft spot, but Christian's floor is simply higher, and Week 1 rewards the roster that doesn't need Saturday injury news to break right.

copies.headline: Two Bottom-Feeders Split Every Position By Inches
copies.body:
Leif projects ahead by a single point, and the gap is entirely in the backfield: McCaffrey and Henry at 35 versus Gibbs and whatever Mitchell scrapes together at 30. The problem is McCaffrey is questionable in a 48.5-total game at the Rams, and behind him Leif's depth is David Montgomery and a pile of eight-point handcuffs. Mitchell's RB2 situation is worse — Rachaad White is questionable, Josh Jacobs is day-to-day at zero, and Kaleb Johnson projects one point. If Gibbs doesn't hit against a Lions offense favored by seven, Mitchell has nothing. Detroit sitting on a lead and feeding Gibbs carries is the friendlier version of that game.
Mitchell wins receiver 39-36 and tight end with Tyler Warren, but Warren is questionable and Colts-Ravens at 48.5 is the best environment either roster has. Leif's edge is Josh Allen, the only genuinely safe player in this matchup, in a 44.5-total game Buffalo is barely favored to win. Kyle Pitts as the only tight end on the roster is a real hole. Nico Collins gets Buffalo's secondary and Mitchell needs him to be the ceiling, but Jaxson Dart chasing points against Dallas is a real path to points.

intro: Six games and four of them are inside two and a half points, led by Leif's 0.8-point edge over Mitchell — a margin that will be decided by whichever kicker gets a garbage-time field goal. Kaleb by 1.4 over Isaac, Grant by 2.4 at CJ, and Christian by 2.1 at Peter aren't much sturdier. The only real separation is John, favored by 8.8 at home against Noah, with Logan's 6.8-point cushion over Adam a distant second.
